headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Admits Affair, Board Investigates Spy Links
summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang has acknowledged an affair with a suspected Chinese government agent. The company's Board of Directors has launched an independent investigation into the matter.
details: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, an AI executive identified as a suspected agent of the Chinese government. The revelation comes as Nvidia's Board of Directors initiates an independent investigation into the relationship.

In a memo to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged his infidelity, stating, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." He expressed remorse for letting his family down and damaging their life together.

Huang pledged full cooperation with the board's investigation, emphasizing his commitment to protecting Nvidia and supporting U.S. national security. He stated, "I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."
The investigation aims to address national security concerns raised by the relationship. Huang requested privacy for his family, stating they bear no responsibility for his choices.

headline: Google Gemini gets PDF editing for files generated in chat
summary: The AI assistant now allows users to open and tweak supported PDFs directly within the chat interface, boosting productivity for Google Workspace users.
details: Google Gemini has integrated a new PDF editing feature, allowing users to modify files generated within the chat or from Google Workspace apps. This enhancement aims to streamline document management and editing tasks for those who primarily use Google's ecosystem.

The in-chat PDF editor works by enabling users to open supported files and provide specific instructions for changes. Users can highlight text or areas within the document and ask Gemini to revise them, offering a more intuitive editing experience than lengthy prompts.

While the PDF editing functionality is available on both mobile and web versions of Gemini, other file format editing (like Docs, Sheets, and code) is primarily limited to the desktop browser. This cross-platform availability makes it convenient for on-the-go edits.

It's important to note that Gemini's PDF editor only supports native files created within the chat or Google Workspace. PDFs generated externally, such as from Adobe Acrobat or scanned images, are not currently supported, which is a limitation for users working with a broader range of documents.

Despite some limitations, such as occasional rendering issues and sluggish processing on mobile, the feature is considered a practical enhancement for casual editing and quick document modifications. Google's continued refinement could turn Gemini into a more robust document management tool.

The ability to generate and edit files directly within Gemini, especially PDFs, offers a compelling alternative to standalone editors for users embedded in the Google ecosystem. This move signifies Gemini's growing utility beyond simple chat interactions.
